task.description: Independently validate REQ-225's design against all 7 acceptance criteria, the 11-rule resolution, canonicalisation-reuse accuracy, and implementation-readiness.

result.note:
HARD FAIL on check 3 (independent rule count). The design doc (lib/letflow/design/req225-entity-definition-schema-validation.md) §3 claims its own arithmetic 'yields the final count of 11' rules, but its own enumeration table (lines 270-283) lists 12 distinct rule identifiers, not 11: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8a, 8b, 8c, 8d, 9 -- that is 7 singly-numbered rules (1-7) + 4 lettered cardinality sub-rules (8a-8d) + 1 (rule 9) = 12. The doc's own derivation is self-contradictory: it computes '9 categories - 1 (cardinality) + 4 (cardinality sub-rules) = 12' correctly, then claims an *additional* fold ('field uniqueness and index/constraint-name uniqueness into one rule, Rule 2') is needed to bring 12 down to 11 -- but AC2's original 9 named categories already contain only ONE uniqueness category ('field uniqueness'; there is no separate 'index/constraint-name uniqueness' category in AC2's list to fold away). The described fold therefore reduces nothing: it merges a category that was never separately counted, so the true total after the cardinality split remains 12, matching the table's actual row count. AC2 requires exactly 11 independently-fixturable rules; this design specifies 12 while asserting 11, which is a real, independently-verifiable miscount, not a labeling nit -- it means REQ-225's own AC2 ('each of the 11 ... rules') cannot be satisfied as designed without either genuinely merging two of the current 12 rule-slots into one (and updating Rule 2 or another rule's scope accordingly) or admitting 12 rules and renegotiating AC2/the requirement text. Per WF-02's zero-partial-credit policy this single failure fails the whole design gate.

Other checks performed, for the record (would have been PASS in isolation, not sufficient to offset the count failure): (1) AC coverage/traceability table (design section 10) matches design content section-by-section, no gaps found besides the count itself. (2) No implementation code -- the two `defmodule ... end` blocks in section 7 contain only @typedoc/@doc/@spec, no `def ... do ... end` bodies; verified via grep for 'def '/'do$' patterns, none found beyond the two module openers. (3) The 11-count claim -- INDEPENDENTLY RECOUNTED AND FOUND WRONG (see FAIL reason above; this was the specific check that failed). (4) Ownership-model decision (tenant-scoped, design §1) is prominent (design's own opening decision section, not buried) and its factual citations verified directly: grepped lib/letflow/repository.ex (takes explicit `prefix`, derives `tenant_id` via TenantProvisioning, no caller-supplied raw tenant_id trusted) and lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex (`register_type/2`, `get_type/2` take `tenant_id :: Ecto.UUID.t()`, resolve physical per-tenant schema) -- both genuinely tenant-scoped as claimed. (5) Canonicalisation reuse verified against the real lib/letflow/repository/canonicaliser.ex: `canonicalize_content/2` (line 102-104, spec `(String.t(), binary()) :: {:ok, canonical_form()} | {:error, :invalid_json}`) and `content_hash/1` (line 131-133, spec `(canonical_form()) :: binary()`) both exist with the exact names/arities the design cites in §4/§7 -- real, no fabricated function. (6) Logical-shape-versioning worked examples traced against the stated rule (strip display_name/description, name-keyed order-insensitive sets for fields/indexes/foreign_keys/constraints) -- all 4 examples (2 non-bumping: field reorder, display_name-only change; 2 bumping: field addition, field type change) are consistent with the stated rule. (7) Module placement -- confirmed via `ls lib/letflow/entities` (does not exist, no conflict) and confirmed the cited precedent module `lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_digest.ex` (Letflow.Definitions.PromotionDigest) actually exists, supporting the design's placement analogy. (8) Cardinality limits (200/32/32/32) -- design §9 item 1 explicitly states these are the design's own chosen numbers (R-Co source unreachable), with stated reasoning ('generous enough not to block any realistic entity type while still being a real, enforceable, testable bound') -- not silently invented. (9) Ambiguity -- aside from the rule-count defect itself (which would force an implementer to silently decide how to reconcile 12 designed rules against AC2's '11' text, exactly the kind of judgment call this gate exists to prevent), no other unresolved signature/error-shape ambiguity was found in §7's `validate/1`/`content_hash/1`/`logical_shape_of/1` specs.

Route back to CODE-DESIGNER with this specific instruction: either (a) genuinely collapse two of the 12 current rule-slots into one (e.g. if index-name-uniqueness and FK/constraint-name-uniqueness really can share one violation atom/rule with field-uniqueness in a way that still lets AC2's 'a fixture that violates only that rule' hold for all three sub-scopes as ONE rule -- but then the cardinality split must drop from 4 sub-rules to 3, or another rule must merge, to land on exactly 11), or (b) if 12 is the honest count, say so plainly and flag to ORCH that REQ-225's AC2 text ('11 numbered structural validation rules') needs REQ-ANALYST/REQ-VALIDATOR reconciliation rather than the design silently asserting an incorrect count of 11 to match already-written requirement text it cannot actually satisfy as designed.
